cues.text: A 45-year-old man has his submandibular salivary gland removed for sialadenitis.
Here the surgeon lifts out the submandibular gland.
The gland was inflamed: that is sialadenitis.
On the first day after the operation, something is wrong.
He drools saliva from the angle of his mouth, on the side of the operation.
The nerve at risk is the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve.
Injury to it paralyses depressor anguli oris, so saliva escapes from the angle of the mouth.
